name: LinkedIn
summary: This guide covers integrating with LinkedIn's OAuth using the Authorization Code (3-legged) OAuth 2.0 flow. LinkedIn offers a shared Composio-managed OAuth application for basic and low-volume use, but production applications (or those needing special scopes, avoiding strict shared quotas, or requiring specific company branding/scopes) are advised to register their own LinkedIn OAuth application via the LinkedIn Developer Portal. The setup involves configuring a LinkedIn app, adding redirect URIs, and obtaining Client ID and Secret, after which LinkedIn members authenticate and consent for your app to access their data.
decision: You should use your own LinkedIn app unless you confirm that the default Composio-managed OAuth meets your rate limit and scope needs. To use your own app, register a LinkedIn application in the LinkedIn Developer Portal, add your redirect URI, configure required products/scopes, and use the issued Client ID and Secret. If Composio-managed OAuth suffices, you can connect without creating an app, but for most production or special-permission use cases, your own app is necessary.

prerequisites.title: LinkedIn Developer Account
prerequisites.body: You must have (or create) a LinkedIn account and access to the LinkedIn Developer Portal.

prerequisites.title: Company Page Association
prerequisites.body: LinkedIn OAuth applications must be associated with a LinkedIn Company Page.

steps.title: Register a LinkedIn Developer Application
steps.body: Log in to the LinkedIn Developer Portal and click 'Create App', then fill out the details (name, company page, logo, etc.).

steps.title: Obtain Client ID and Client Secret
steps.body: After creating the app, go to the Auth tab to view/copy your Client ID and Client Secret (called Primary Client Secret in LinkedIn).

steps.title: Configure Redirect URI
steps.body: In the LinkedIn app's Auth tab, add your redirect URI (must start with HTTPS, be absolute, and match exactly the URI used in your integration).

steps.title: Enable Products and Scopes
steps.body: Add required Products such as 'Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect' and any API scopes. Apply for new products/scopes as needed under the Products tab.
steps.note: Different APIs/tools require different scopes; see LinkedIn and Composio documentation for needed permissions.

steps.title: Integrate OAuth Flow
steps.body: Direct the user's browser to LinkedIn's authorization endpoint with required query params: response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri, state, scope. On approval, exchange code for access token.
steps.note: All authentication is performed securely on LinkedIn's domain; browser redirected to your app after consent. The citation is not an official documentation host.

steps.title: Test the OAuth Integration
steps.body: After connecting, perform basic OAuth flow (log in, approval screen, callback to redirect_uri) and complete connection in the integration platform.
steps.note: LinkedIn and third-party docs refer to testing/manually authorizing to confirm flow.

blockers.title: Missing Company Page
blockers.body: You cannot register an OAuth application without associating it to a LinkedIn Company Page.

blockers.title: Unapproved Scopes or Products
blockers.body: Access to certain API scopes requires explicit application review/approval by LinkedIn, and the app will not work for those scopes until approval is granted.
blockers.note: The citation is not an official documentation host.

human_actions.title: Create or access LinkedIn Developer account and Company Page
human_actions.body: Log into LinkedIn and create a Developer account and Company Page if not already available.

human_actions.title: Register LinkedIn App and enter app details
human_actions.body: Manually create and fill out the LinkedIn app registration form, including company page and branding.

human_actions.title: Add redirect URI to LinkedIn OAuth app
human_actions.body: Copy and paste the provided redirect URI from your integration platform (e.g., Composio or your server) into your LinkedIn app settings.

human_actions.title: Copy Client ID and Secret
human_actions.body: Manually retrieve and save your LinkedIn app's Client ID and Secret; enter them in your integration platform or environment (never share secrets publicly).

human_actions.title: Consent to requested scopes and complete OAuth login
human_actions.body: Manually authorize the app as a LinkedIn member when prompted during the OAuth flow.
